stem: Why is a stock-market investment not insurable as a risk?
options: It is a speculative risk that can produce a gain as well as a loss
why: Only pure risks, with no chance of gain, are insurable.

stem: A health policy has a 15% co-pay and the admissible claim is Rs 2,00,000. How much does the insurer pay?
why: The insured bears 15% (Rs 30,000) and the insurer pays the balance of Rs 1,70,000.

stem: After paying a car claim, the insurer recovers the amount from the driver who caused the accident. This right is called:
why: Subrogation lets the insurer step into the insured's shoes against the party at fault.

stem: Three years after a life policy was issued, can the insurer reject a death claim for non-disclosure?
options: No, under section 45 it cannot be called in question on any ground
Only if the premium was paid late
why: Section 45 makes a life policy unquestionable after three years from issue, risk start or revival.

stem: Which policy is an example of defined-benefit rather than indemnity insurance?
options: Critical illness cover paying a lump sum on diagnosis
why: Critical illness pays a fixed sum regardless of actual expense; the others reimburse actual loss.

stem: Which life insurance product provides the largest cover for the lowest premium?
why: Term cover has no savings element, so premiums buy only protection.

stem: A Rs 10 lakh endowment policy with 50 half-yearly premiums becomes paid-up after 10 premiums. What is the paid-up sum assured?
A life policy bought under the Married Women's Property Act can name as beneficiaries:
options: Wife and/or children only, and they cannot be changed later
why: MWPA policies benefit wife and children, are beyond creditors, and beneficiaries are fixed.

stem: When expected income growth equals the return on invested insurance proceeds, human life value equals:
options: Current annual income times years left to retirement
why: With a zero real discount rate, HLV is simply income multiplied by remaining working years.

stem: For a life policy with term over 10 years bought by someone under 45, the minimum sum assured is:
why: IRDAI requires at least 10 times annual premium below age 45 (7 times above) for terms beyond 10 years.

stem: Which motor cover is compulsory for a car driven on public roads in India?
why: Third-party liability insurance is mandatory; own-damage is optional.

stem: How does a super top-up health plan differ from a top-up plan?
options: Its deductible applies to the total claims in a year rather than to each claim
It can only be bought from the employer
why: Super top-ups aggregate claims against the threshold; top-ups test each claim separately.

stem: A car owner with a no-claim bonus sells the car and buys a new one. The bonus:
options: Can be transferred to the owner's new car
Goes to the buyer of the old car
why: No-claim bonus belongs to the insured, not the vehicle.

stem: An employer that wants protection against employees committing fraud with company cash should buy:
why: Fidelity insurance covers losses from employee dishonesty.

stem: Why does holding two separate hospitalisation policies rarely increase what you can recover for one illness?
options: Indemnity cover can never pay more than the actual bill
why: Indemnity policies reimburse actual loss only; defined-benefit covers can each pay in full.

stem: Why is retirement considered a unique goal compared with buying a house or educating a child?
options: There is no loan available to fund it
It is fully funded by the government
why: Lenders finance homes and education, but nobody lends for retirement.

stem: At 6% inflation, monthly expenses of Rs 60,000 today will cost about how much in 10 years?
Underestimating how long a person will live after retiring creates which risk?
why: Longevity risk is the danger of outliving the retirement corpus.

stem: The replacement ratio method of estimating retirement income assumes the retiree needs:
options: A fixed percentage of pre-retirement income, grown with inflation
Exactly the same rupee income forever
Income equal to the provident fund balance
why: A share of final income (say 70 to 80%) is targeted and then increased each year for inflation.

stem: Why can an employer not simply pay superannuation pensions out of each year's profits?
options: Retirees would depend on the employer's future finances, so annuities must be bought from a life insurer
why: Pay-as-you-go pensions are not permitted; benefits must be funded and provided through insurers.

stem: Of the employer's 12% EPF contribution, what portion goes to the Employees' Pension Scheme (on wages up to Rs 15,000)?
why: 8.33% goes to EPS and the remaining 3.67% to the EPF account.

stem: An employee covered by the Gratuity Act retires after 15 years with last drawn basic plus DA of Rs 40,000 a month. Gratuity under the formula is about:
What is the maximum that can be deposited in the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme?
why: The SCSS ceiling is Rs 30 lakh per individual.

stem: A non-government NPS subscriber exits at 60 with a corpus of Rs 50 lakh. Under the December 2025 exit rules, what is the minimum that must buy an annuity?
why: Non-government subscribers annuitise at least 20% on normal exit (government subscribers 40%).

stem: In a systematic withdrawal plan, a rise in NAV means each fixed withdrawal:
why: A fixed rupee amount needs fewer units at a higher NAV.

stem: Putting away roughly Rs 3,376 every month from age 30 grows to Rs 1.18 crore at 60 when returns are 12%. Starting the same plan at age 40, roughly what monthly amount is required?
why: With only 20 years of compounding the requirement rises to about Rs 11,928 a month.

stem: When changing jobs with an EPF balance after three years of service, what is generally better?
options: Transfer it to the new employer's account through the UAN
why: Transferring avoids tax on early withdrawal, counts past service, and keeps compounding.

stem: Increasing a SIP by a set percentage every year is called:
why: Step-up SIPs raise contributions as income grows.

stem: For a retiree beyond 75, the primary criteria for choosing products are:
options: Capital protection, steady income and liquidity
why: In late retirement the horizon is short, so safety, income and liquidity dominate.

stem: When is a natural moment for an adviser to raise charitable giving with a client?
options: Only when the client is in debt
Never, as it is not financial planning
During a liquidity event such as selling a business or receiving an inheritance
why: Liquidity events, will-writing and life events naturally prompt philanthropy conversations.

stem: An Indian citizen returns after 20 years abroad and stays the whole year in India. For the first year, what is his likely tax status?
why: Non-residency in 9 of the past 10 years makes him RNOR even though he is resident.

stem: Under the new regime for FY 2025-26, a resident individual with total income of Rs 12 lakh (no special-rate income) pays tax of:
options: Nil, because of the section 87A rebate
why: The 87A rebate of up to Rs 60,000 makes tax nil up to Rs 12 lakh in the new regime.

stem: A husband gifts Rs 30 lakh to his wife, who invests it and earns Rs 1.5 lakh interest. The interest is taxed in the hands of:
why: Income from assets transferred to a spouse without adequate consideration is clubbed with the transferor.

stem: A long-term capital loss can be set off against:
why: LTCL offsets only LTCG; STCL can offset both.

stem: Under the old regime, the maximum deduction for home-loan interest on a self-occupied house is:
why: Self-occupied interest is capped at Rs 2 lakh in the old regime and not allowed in the new regime.

stem: Listed equity shares become long-term capital assets after being held for more than:
why: Listed shares and equity fund units are long-term after more than 12 months.

stem: Units of a debt mutual fund (more than 65% in debt) bought in June 2024 and sold in 2027 are taxed as:
options: Short-term gains at slab rates, regardless of holding period
why: Specified mutual funds bought from April 2023 are always short-term under section 50AA.

stem: Under section 54EC, long-term gains on land or building can be exempted by investing in specified bonds up to:
why: 54EC caps the investment at Rs 50 lakh, made within six months.

stem: Which transaction is NOT treated as a transfer for capital gains?
options: Receiving shares under a gift from a parent
why: Gifts and inheritances are excluded from transfer; the recipient takes the donor's cost.

stem: A resident individual sells, in 2025, a house bought in 2011. How may the long-term gain be taxed?
options: At the lower of 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation
why: Land or buildings acquired before 23 July 2024 allow residents the lower of the two computations.

stem: From 1 October 2024, the money a shareholder receives in a company's buyback is taxed as:
options: Dividend income, with the share cost treated as a capital loss
why: Buyback proceeds are deemed dividends; the cost becomes a capital loss.

stem: A friend gifts listed shares worth Rs 80,000 (no other gifts that year). How much is taxable for the recipient?
why: Once the year's gifts from non-relatives exceed Rs 50,000, the whole amount is taxable.

stem: Which person is NOT a relative for the gift-tax exemption?
why: Cousins, nephews, nieces and step-siblings are not relatives for this purpose.

stem: Dividends from shares received by a resident individual are taxed:
options: At the individual's slab rate under income from other sources
why: Since DDT was abolished, dividends are taxed in shareholders' hands at slab rates.

stem: Which receipt is exempt from tax regardless of amount?
options: Cash gifts received on one's own marriage
A Rs 1 lakh gift from a colleague
why: Gifts on the occasion of the recipient's marriage are fully exempt.

stem: The gain on a 91-day treasury bill held to maturity is taxed as:
options: Short-term capital gain at slab rates
why: T-bills are issued at a discount; the gain is short-term capital gain at normal rates.

stem: For tax-free bonds, which statement is correct?
options: Both interest and capital gains are exempt
Interest is taxable but gains are exempt
Interest is exempt, but gains on sale or redemption are taxable
Neither is taxed only for NRIs
why: Only the interest is exempt; capital gains follow normal bond rules.

stem: Gains on a market-linked debenture held for three years are taxed as:
why: Section 50AA treats all MLD gains as short-term regardless of holding.

stem: A resident earns Rs 5 lakh of mutual fund dividends and paid Rs 1.5 lakh interest on money borrowed to invest. How much interest can be deducted?
why: The interest deduction is capped at 20% of the dividend, so Rs 1 lakh.

stem: To claim a lower tax rate under a tax treaty, a non-resident must generally provide:
options: A tax residency certificate and Form 10F
why: DTAA relief needs a TRC from the home country plus Form 10F.

stem: Short-term gains on listed shares sold on an exchange after 23 July 2024, with STT paid, are taxed at:
why: Section 111A gains are taxed at 20% for transfers from 23 July 2024.

stem: Shares bought in 2017 for Rs 100 had a fair market value of Rs 200 on 31 January 2018 and were sold in 2025 for Rs 150. What is the long-term gain per share?
why: Cost = higher of 100 and lower of (200, 150) = 150, so the gain is nil.

stem: Profits and losses from trading exchange-traded futures and options are generally treated as:
why: Exchange-traded derivatives are excluded from speculation, so they are normal business income.

stem: Bonus-stripping rules disallow the loss on original units when they were bought within three months before the record date and sold within:
why: The loss is ignored if sold within nine months after the record date while holding the bonus units.

stem: Which is NOT deductible when computing capital gains on shares sold through an exchange?
why: STT and CTT cannot be deducted in computing capital gains.

stem: An employee exercises 100 ESOPs at Rs 500 when the fair value is Rs 6,500. What is the taxable perquisite?
why: Perquisite = (6,500 - 500) x 100 = Rs 6,00,000, taxed as salary.

stem: An individual who holds a Sovereign Gold Bond to maturity and redeems it with RBI pays capital gains tax of:
why: Redemption of SGBs by individuals is not a transfer, so the gain is exempt.

stem: Which statement about a REIT distribution of rent to unitholders is correct?
options: It is taxed in the REIT and exempt for unitholders
It is exempt in the REIT and taxable for unitholders
why: Rental income has pass-through status: exempt for the REIT and taxable in unitholders' hands.

stem: For a non-ULIP life policy issued after 1 April 2023 with annual premium of Rs 6 lakh, maturity proceeds are:
options: Fully exempt because sum assured is ten times premium
Exempt only if the insured dies
Taxable as other income after deducting premiums paid
why: Aggregate premiums above Rs 5 lakh remove the 10(10D) exemption for such policies.

stem: Category I and II AIFs are pass-through for tax on all income except:
why: Business income is taxed in the fund; other income passes through to investors.

stem: An investor bought 1,000 shares at Rs 150. After a 1:2 split (one share becomes two), what is the cost per share?
why: The original Rs 1.5 lakh is spread over 2,000 shares, Rs 75 each, with the original holding date.

stem: Bonus shares allotted in September 2023 and sold in August 2024 at Rs 120 give what kind of gain?
options: Long-term gain on cost of Rs 120
Short-term gain on the full sale price, since cost is nil and holding counts from allotment
Long-term gain on cost equal to the original shares
why: Bonus shares cost nil and their holding period starts at allotment.

stem: A shareholder renounces rights entitlements for Rs 200 each. How is the gain taxed?
options: Short-term at slab rates, with cost of the rights taken as nil
why: Renounced rights have nil cost and are not equity shares, so slab rates apply.

stem: Under the new regime for FY 2025-26, what is the tax (before cess) on total income of Rs 15 lakh?
Lending shares under SEBI's securities lending and borrowing scheme:
options: Is not a transfer, and the lending fee is taxed as income
Triggers capital gains on the lent shares
why: SLB lending is excluded from transfer; the fee is business or other income.

stem: Who among these is NOT a Class I heir of a Hindu male dying intestate?
why: The father is a Class II heir; mother, widow, sons and daughters are Class I.

stem: A Hindu man dies intestate leaving a widow, two sons and his mother. How is his estate shared?
options: Widow takes half, the rest equally
Each of the four takes an equal one-quarter share
why: Widow, each son and the mother each take one share as Class I heirs.

stem: Under Muslim personal law, how much of the net estate may a person bequeath by will?
why: A Muslim can bequeath at most one-third; the rest passes to heirs.

stem: Intestate succession among Christians is governed by:
why: The Indian Succession Act governs Christians' testamentary and intestate succession.

stem: What does mutation of a property in revenue records establish?
options: The person liable for property tax; it is not proof of title
why: Mutation updates revenue records for tax collection but does not confer title.

stem: A document used to make a small change to an existing will is called a:
why: A codicil alters or adds to a will and must be executed like a will.

stem: Probate is mandatory where a will concerns immovable property located in:
options: Kolkata, or the municipal limits of Chennai or Mumbai
why: Probate is compulsory for wills made in, or covering property in, the old presidency towns.

stem: Registration of a will in India is:
options: Optional; an unregistered will is valid
Required within six months of death
why: The Registration Act makes registration optional, though it helps prevent tampering.

stem: A private trust where trustees decide how much each beneficiary gets is generally taxed:
options: At the maximum marginal rate, subject to exceptions
why: Discretionary trusts are taxed at MMR unless an exception applies.

stem: Two people own a flat as joint tenants. One dies. His share:
options: Passes automatically to the surviving joint tenant
why: Joint tenancy carries a right of survivorship, unlike tenancy in common.

stem: Prospect theory suggests that people:
options: Weigh losses more heavily than equal gains
Value wealth only in absolute terms
why: Gains and losses are judged against a reference point and losses hurt more.

stem: Selling winning stocks too early while holding losing stocks too long is known as the:
why: The disposition effect stems from loss aversion and regret avoidance.

stem: An investor treats a bonus as 'fun money' to gamble but guards salary carefully. This illustrates:
why: Mental accounting treats money differently depending on its source or label.

stem: Insisting a stock is cheap because it once traded far higher is an example of:
why: The old price acts as an anchor that distorts judgement of value.

stem: Behavioural biases are broadly divided into:
why: Cognitive errors come from faulty reasoning; emotional biases from feelings, and are harder to correct.

stem: An Indian investor keeps all equity in Indian stocks because they feel familiar. This is:
why: Home bias overweights domestic assets and gives up global diversification.

stem: Moving money every year into last year's top-performing fund is an example of:
why: Investors extrapolate recent winners, which tends to buy high.

stem: Which is a practical way to stop clients from overtrading during volatile markets?
options: Agree written ground rules for action in advance
why: Pre-agreed rules act as commitments that counter action bias.

stem: A client buys an endowment policy mainly to save tax. What is the typical result?
options: Too little life cover at a high cost
why: Tax-driven insurance buying usually ends with inadequate cover and poor returns.

stem: A client holds fourteen equity mutual funds with heavily overlapping portfolios. What is the main problem?
options: Clutter and duplicated holdings that add complexity without real extra diversification
why: Over-diversification across similar funds adds cost and confusion without reducing risk further.

stem: All else equal, which change would usually increase a client's capacity to take investment risk?
options: Higher capital base and stable income
why: Larger wealth and steady income raise the ability to absorb losses.

stem: Under SEBI rules, when must an investment adviser complete a client's risk profile?
why: Risk profiling must precede advice, and free trials need the profile communicated and accepted.

stem: Asset allocation that changes only when the client's goals or circumstances change is called:
why: Strategic allocation follows goals and risk profile, rebalanced back to target.

stem: Which objective is best met by cash and short-term bank deposits?
why: Cash and short deposits give liquidity and safety, not growth.

stem: Why might a risk-profile questionnaire produce misleading results?
options: Clients may guess the answer they think is right rather than answer honestly
why: There are no right answers, and guessing undermines the profile; tools must be used judiciously.

stem: Compared with an index fund, an index ETF typically:
options: Is bought from the AMC at end-of-day NAV
Trades on the exchange at live prices, with brokerage and bid-ask spreads
why: ETFs trade like shares; index funds transact with the AMC at NAV.

stem: Which gold investment pays periodic interest?
why: SGBs pay 2.5% a year on issue value in addition to gold-linked redemption.

stem: What is the minimum investment for a Category III AIF?
why: AIF minimum is Rs 1 crore versus Rs 50 lakh for PMS and as little as Rs 1,000 for mutual funds.

stem: Which statement about ELSS compared with PPF is correct?
options: ELSS has a shorter lock-in but market-linked returns
why: ELSS locks in for 3 years with equity risk; PPF locks in 15 years with sovereign-backed returns.

stem: Compared with a debenture of the same company, a company fixed deposit is usually:
why: Deposits are unsecured, so they typically pay a little more than secured debentures.

stem: Investment return is 9% and inflation 6%. The inflation-adjusted (real) rate used to compute a retirement corpus is about:
Ms T invests Rs 60,000 in an asset yielding 10%, financing it with borrowings of 1.4 times her own money at 9%. What is her return on her own funds?
why: Own funds 25,000, borrowings 35,000, interest 3,150, gain 6,000, net 2,850, so 2,850 / 25,000 = 11.4%.

stem: Adil needs Rs 25,000 a month for his family for 30 years (8% return, 6% inflation, corpus about Rs 68 lakh), plus Rs 30 lakh to clear a loan and Rs 10 lakh for his child. He has Rs 50 lakh of cover. How much more life cover does he need?
why: 68 + 30 + 10 - 50 = about Rs 58 lakh.

stem: A grandmother in her late 60s wants to build a fund for a five-year-old grandchild's college education. Which fund suits best?
options: A large and mid-cap equity fund, given the long horizon
why: The goal's horizon, not the grandmother's age, decides the equity exposure.

stem: A mother's registered will leaves her house to her son. Can the son pledge the house for a loan now, citing the will?
options: Yes, because the will is registered
Yes, because he is a Class I heir
Only with his sister's written consent
No, because a will takes effect only on death and can be changed until then
why: A will confers no rights during the testator's lifetime.
